title: bonsai.buglist/1
description: bonsai bug --json (contract §10, §7.3; plan P-T-6023, step 6): the bugs bonsai bug list printed, the one bonsai bug show printed, or the one a writing subcommand (add, fix, wontfix, watch, reopen, edit) wrote, each with its file in the main checkout's bug folder (bonsai.yaml's documents.bug) and its frontmatter as bonsai.bug/1 holds it. Printed, never stored. Written by bonsai bug with --json; read by agents and the studio. On a refusal bugs and malformed are [] and error says why. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

workspace.description: The workspace: its id and name from bonsai.yaml, and the main checkout's absolute path, forward slashes (printed locally, never stored or forwarded); null when the command refused before reading bonsai.yaml.

root.description: The checkout's absolute path, forward slashes.

command.description: The subcommand that ran: list, show, add, fix, wontfix, watch, reopen or edit (bonsai bug --help lists them); null when the command refused before one was read.

bugs.description: The bugs, for list in id order (by number, oldest first) and only those its filters keep; for show the one asked for; for a writing subcommand the one it wrote, as written. [] on a refusal.

bug.title: The settings page forgets the dark mode switch after a restart
bug.fixed_in: 0a1b2c3d (the switch is saved before the page closes)

items.description: One bug: its file, its frontmatter and, for show and every writing subcommand, its body.

path.description: The bug file, project-relative in the main checkout, forward slashes: in the folder bonsai.yaml names under documents.bug, named <id>.md or <id>-<slug>.md.

bug.description: Its frontmatter as bonsai.bug/1 holds it: format first, then id, title, status (open, fixed, wontfix or watched), area, where, found_by, filed_by, fixed_by, fixed_in, task, was, why, created, closed and labels, then any field this Bonsai does not know. An open object here, whose home is bonsai.bug/1 (the schema checker has no $ref).

examples.title: The settings page forgets the dark mode switch after a restart
examples.fixed_in: 0a1b2c3d (the switch is saved before the page closes)

body.description: Its body, the markdown after the frontmatter (how to repeat it, what was seen, notes), line endings LF; "" for none; null for list, which prints headers only.
examples: **How to repeat it:** turn dark mode on, close the game, open it again: the switch reads off.

malformed.description: A file in the bug folder named by a bug id that does not read as bonsai.bug/1 (bonsai check names it as a finding): its path and why. One bad file never blocks the rest. [] for none, and for every subcommand but list and show.

examples.reason: its status "closed" is not one of open, fixed, wontfix, watched

path.description: The file, project-relative in the main checkout, forward slashes.

reason.description: Why it does not read, one sentence, ASCII.
examples: its frontmatter has no closing --- line

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
